questions.q: What did Phineas Gage's accident reveal about the brain?
a: Damage to certain areas can change personality and emotions
The brain can recover fully from any physical injury
Emotions are stored separately from the thinking brain
Personality remains fixed no matter what happens to the brain
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the rod injury left Gage impulsive and unlike his former self.

questions.q: What puzzled Damasio about his patient Elliot?
a: He felt no emotions and also struggled to make decisions
He felt too much emotion to discuss his past
He could not remember any of his earlier life
He refused to talk about the accident at all
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that losing emotion did not make Elliot more rational; it made reasoning harder.

a: Emotional shortcuts built from past experience that speed up choices
Physical exercises that improve concentration
Medical tests that measure brain damage
Memories that have no emotional content at all
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes them as feelings attached to options, drawn from your history.

questions.q: What did Elliot's half-hour of deliberating over an appointment show?
a: Without emotional input, reasoning can go around in circles
He cared too much about choosing the perfect time
He had forgotten how calendars work
He was trying to avoid meeting the author
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses the story to show that feelings are part of logical thinking.

questions.q: What is the "error" in Descartes' Error?
a: Treating the mind and body as separate, with emotion outside reason
Believing that the body has any influence on the mind
Claiming that brain injuries cannot affect behavior
Assuming that all decisions are made consciously
questions.why: The overview says Damasio attacks the idea that mind and body are disconnected.
